questions.q: With the default logits Cat $= 2$, Dog $= -1$, Car $= 0.5$ and $T = 1$, what is (approximately) $P(\text{Cat})$?
questions.explain: $\frac{e^{2}}{e^{2} + e^{-1} + e^{0.5}} = \frac{7.39}{7.39 + 0.37 + 1.65} \approx 0.786$. Dividing raw scores by their sum gives $2/1.5 \approx 1.33$ — not even a valid probability.

questions.q: Why does Softmax exponentiate instead of simply dividing the raw scores by their sum?
options: $e^z$ makes every value strictly positive (raw sums can give negative probabilities or divide by zero) and exaggerates differences
Because dividing by the sum would not add up to 1
questions.explain: A logit of $-2$ would give a negative "probability", and scores like $2$ and $-2$ sum to $0$. Exponentiating fixes both and widens gaps ($e^2 = 7.39$ vs. $e^1 = 2.72$).

questions.q: Real implementations compute Softmax of $z_i - \max_j z_j$. What does this change about the output?
options: It makes the largest probability exactly 1
It changes the ranking of the classes
Nothing — adding the same constant to every logit cancels out, but it prevents overflow
questions.explain: $\frac{e^{z_i - c}}{\sum_j e^{z_j - c}} = \frac{e^{z_i}}{\sum_j e^{z_j}}$ because $e^{-c}$ cancels. With $c = \max z$ the largest exponent is $e^0 = 1$, so $e^{1000}$ never overflows to `inf`.

questions.q: Raising the temperature from $T = 1$ to $T = 5$ (dividing every logit by $T$) does what to the probabilities?
options: Makes them softer — closer to uniform
Pushes them toward argmax (one-hot on the top class)
Makes them sum to more than 1
questions.explain: Dividing by a large $T$ shrinks the gaps between logits, so $P(\text{Cat})$ falls from $\approx 0.79$ to $\approx 0.44$ here. Low $T$ (e.g. $0.5$) sharpens toward argmax instead.
